claims.text: Signed the 24 June 2009 letter to Deputy Secretary of Defense William J. Lynn III, on Senate Majority Leader letterhead, requesting DoD place the AAITP under 'Restricted Special Access Protection'.

DIA records him as co-sponsor with Senator Daniel Inouye (D-HI) of the language in the July 2008 Supplemental Appropriation bill directing DIA to investigate foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats 'from the present out to 40 years in the future' — a $10 million add.

DIA Talking Paper: 'Senator Reid has a deep interest in the potential threat posed by unconventional aerospace technologies; that is, technologies that are a radical departure to those used in current advanced aerospace vehicles. He is interested in what technological "leaps" are feasible and their implications to US national defense.'

Met DIA leadership on the program at least four documented times: 13 Nov 2008 (with the DIA Director), 5 Jan 2009, mid-May 2009, and 19 Nov 2009 at Senate Visitor Center SVC-217 with the Deputy Secretary of Defense present.
AARO Vol. I attributes the FY2008/FY2010 $22M appropriations to his direction as Senate Majority Leader.

claims.source: AARO Historical Record Report Volume 1, 8 March 2024, p.22
claims.text: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats.'

claims.text: Reid requested a 'Restricted Special-Access-Program (SAP) with a Bigoted Access List for specific portions of the AATIP', naming as protectable the methodologies for identifying and engineering advanced technologies and the involvement of private contractors and industry partners.

DIA scheduled a 19 Nov 2009 4:45pm briefing of Reid in SVC-217 to tell him the deliverables 'do not meet the criteria as specified in DoD 5200.1-R to justify the additional protection provided by a SAP.'

claims.text: Reid's insistence on a bigoted access list for 'engineering advanced technologies' and 'involvement of private contractors' indicates he had been told something about reverse-engineering activity that does not appear anywhere in the unclassified DIRD deliverables — the reasoning being that no SAP is needed to protect 38 unclassified academic literature reviews, and DIA said exactly that in refusing him.

connections.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
connections.note: This is the cleanest demonstration that the two small groups are different sets. 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(2) includes the majority and minority leaders of the Senate. 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and 119(g) do not; they reach only committee and subcommittee chairs and ranking members. A Senate Majority Leader has no statutory entitlement to waived DoD SAP notification by virtue of that office. In 2009 the Senate armed services and appropriations seats were held by Levin, McCain, Inouye and Cochran.

label: Harry M. Reid
narrative: Reid is the appropriator who created the funded lineage and then tried to seal it. As Majority Leader he worked with Appropriations chairman Daniel Inouye and Ted Stevens in 2007 to direct roughly $22 million into the defense black budget for what became AAWSAP at DIA — AARO's own 2024 report states flatly that 'at the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA.' Reid took repeated DIA briefings on contract status: talking papers survive from January 2009, May 2009 and November 2009. On 24 June 2009 he wrote to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that portions of what he called the 'Advanced Aerospace Threat and Identification Program' be placed in a Restricted Special Access Program with a bigoted access list, protecting methodologies for identifying and engineering advanced technologies, personnel and oversight details, and the involvement of private contractors and industry partners. That letter is the most important single document in this domain because it establishes that the Senate Majority Leader believed the program was producing something warranting SAP protection with a compartmented access list. DoD refused. Reid later said publicly that $22 million was not enough and that failing to study the subject would be malpractice, and called the program one of the good things he did in his congressional service. He died 28 December 2021.
